concepts.def: The Holy Spirit descended on the disciples, Peter preached to the crowds, and about three thousand were baptised - the birth of the Church.
Acts 2:42-47 describes believers devoted to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer, sharing their possessions in common.
One of seven chosen to serve the community, Stephen's speech to the Sanhedrin in Acts 7 led to his stoning, witnessed by Saul.
An encounter with the risen Christ on the Damascus road transformed Saul from persecutor of the Church into the apostle Paul.
Peter's vision and the baptism of Cornelius in Acts 10, followed by Paul's missionary journeys, carried the gospel beyond Judaism.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Early Church: The Church in Acts — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Early Church: The Church in Acts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Early Church: The Church in Acts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What happened at Pentecost in Acts 2?
options: The Holy Spirit came upon the disciples, Peter preached, and about three thousand people were baptised
Jesus ascended into heaven
Saul was converted on the Damascus road
The Temple in Jerusalem was destroyed

mcqs.q: Who was the first Christian martyr?
options: Stephen
Peter
James
Paul

mcqs.q: What did the Council of Jerusalem in Acts 15 decide?
options: Gentile converts did not need to be circumcised or keep the whole Jewish Law
The Church should remain entirely Jewish
Paul should stop his missionary journeys
The gospels should be written in Hebrew

mcqs.q: What happened to Saul on the road to Damascus?
options: He was blinded by a light, heard the voice of Jesus and was converted
He was arrested by Roman soldiers
He met Peter for the first time
He was shipwrecked

mcqs.q: Did Paul write the Acts of the Apostles?
options: Paul wrote Acts because he is its main character.
Acts was written by Peter as his memoirs.
No - Acts is traditionally attributed to Luke, the author of the third Gospel, as the second volume of his work addressed to Theophilus.
At Pentecost the disciples were given the gift of prophecy about Rome's fall.

mcqs.q: Was the early Church free of disagreement?
options: The early Church had no leaders, so there was nothing to disagree about.
The first Christians always agreed and never argued.
At Pentecost the disciples were given the gift of prophecy about Rome's fall.
No - Acts records real disputes: the complaint of the Hellenist widows in Acts 6, the circumcision controversy settled at Jerusalem in Acts 15, and the split between Paul and Barnabas.

mcqs.q: At Pentecost, did the disciples speak meaningless ecstatic sounds?
options: Pentecost was an outburst of unintelligible babbling that no one could understand.
Acts was written by Peter as his memoirs.
Acts 2 describes them speaking in other real languages that visiting pilgrims understood, each hearing in their own tongue.
At Pentecost the disciples were given the gift of prophecy about Rome's fall.
